summary: Menu cursor count measurer (__thiscall): loads the menu text pointer from field this+0xE0 (falling back to the global byte_5EA438), computes its length plus the terminator, then walks the cursor index forward one step at a time via MenuCursorNavigationHelper, counting each reachable cursor position (starting at 1) until the helper returns the same index (no movement) or reaches the final text position whose preceding character is a non-(-1) terminator, and returns the total number of cursor positions.

local_names.v2: menu text pointer loaded from field this+0xE0, falling back to byte_5EA438
local_names.i: current cursor index passed to the navigation helper
local_names.v6: next cursor index returned by MenuCursorNavigationHelper

operations.description: v2 = *this[56] loads the menu text pointer stored at field this+0xE0.
When the field pointer is null, fall back to the global default text source byte_5EA438.
v3 = strlen(v2) + 1 computes the text length including the terminating character.
v4 = 1 seeds the cursor position count at one before the loop.
Iterate the cursor index i starting at 0; each iteration advances i to the helper's returned index v6 until a break condition is met.
v6 = MenuCursorNavigationHelper(this, i) advances the cursor from index i to the next navigation position.
Break when the helper returns the same index (i == v6, no movement) or when v6 is the final text position (v6 == v3 - 1) and the preceding character v2[v6 - 1] is not the -1 terminator character.
++v4 increments the cursor position count on every reachable position.
Return the total number of cursor positions v4.
Called by BoundedCounterUpdate, sub_47BCF0, UtilityFunction_bd90 and sub_47BE00 to measure the cursor position range of a menu.

unresolved: The navigation semantics of MenuCursorNavigationHelper (0x0047B730) and the meaning of the -1 terminator character are inferred from usage and resolved in the helper's own function.
Whether the count includes the final cursor position depends on the helper's boundary behavior, which is outside this packet.
